intent: Show the reactions a bubble received as a small pill overlapping one of its edges.
typical_uses: A row of reaction emoji with an overflow count on a received turn
A row of reaction buttons the reader can toggle

dont_use_when.situation: A status, tag or count shown on its own rather than anchored to a bubble

invariants.text: The pill is absolutely positioned against its Bubble (position relative) and shifted 75% of its own height past the `side` edge, so it overlaps the bubble and extends into the space above or below it.
`align="start"` insets the pill var(--space-3) from the left edge and `align="end"` from the right edge; these are physical sides and do not mirror under a right-to-left direction.
When any descendant is a `button`, the pill drops its own padding and sits flush around the buttons, which size themselves.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave a row of emoji spans and counts without an accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the row `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that reads the reactions once, or render real buttons with their own names when the reactions are interactive

anti_patterns.dont: Stack bubbles carrying reactions with the default gap between them
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave extra vertical space between those rows, since the pill extends past the bubble edge into it

rtl.by: bubble.module.css .alignStart/.alignEnd inset the pill with physical left/right, so it does not mirror under a right-to-left direction

good.title: Reactions named once for assistive tech, anchored top start
good.code: Ship it. 🔥 +8

bad.title: Reactions placed outside the bubble
bad.why: The pill is positioned absolutely against its Bubble; outside one it anchors to whatever positioned ancestor happens to be nearest.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof bubbleReactionsVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The class-name builder BubbleReactions uses for its `side` and `align` classes; it does not set the `data-side` and `data-align` attributes the component itself renders.
